verses.greek: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν εὑρηκέναι Ἀβραὰμ τὸν προπάτορα ἡμῶν κατὰ σάρκα;
verses.literal: What then will we say to have discovered Abraham the ancestor of us according to the flesh?
verses.dgt: What then shall we say that Abraham our forefather according to the flesh has found?

verses.greek: εἰ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ἔχει καύχημα· ἀλλʼ οὐ πρὸς θεόν,
verses.literal: If for Abraham by works was justified he has ground of boasting but not toward God.
verses.dgt: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about—but not before God.

verses.greek: τί γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει; Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
verses.literal: What for the Scripture says? Believed then Abraham the in God and it was reckoned to him for righteousness.
verses.dgt: For what does Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.”

verses.greek: τῷ δὲ ἐργαζομένῳ ὁ μισθὸς οὐ λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν ἀλλὰ κατὰ ὀφείλημα·
verses.literal: To the one now working the reward not is reckoned according to grace but according to debt
verses.dgt: Now to the one who works, the wage is not counted according to grace but according to what is owed.

verses.greek: τῷ δὲ μὴ ἐργαζομένῳ, πιστεύοντι δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἀσεβῆ, λογίζεται ἡ πίστις αὐτοῦ εἰς δικαιοσύνην,
verses.literal: To the one however not working believing however on the One justifying the ungodly is reckoned the faith of him for righteousness.
verses.dgt: But to the one who does not work but believes in the one who justifies the ungodly, that person’s faith is counted as righteousness,

verses.greek: καθάπερ καὶ Δαυὶδ λέγει τὸν μακαρισμὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ᾧ ὁ θεὸς λογίζεται δικαιοσύνην χωρὶς ἔργων·
verses.literal: just as also David declares the blessedness of the man to whom the God credits righteousness apart from works:
verses.dgt: just as David also speaks of the blessedness of the person to whom God counts righteousness apart from works:

verses.greek: Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι καὶ ὧν ἐπεκαλύφθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι,
verses.literal: Blessed are they of whom are forgiven the lawless deeds and of whom are covered the sins
verses.dgt: “Blessed are those whose lawless deeds were forgiven and whose sins were covered;

verses.greek: μακάριος ἀνὴρ οὗ οὐ μὴ λογίσηται κύριος ἁμαρτίαν.
verses.literal: blessed is the man of whom certainly not may reckon the Lord sin.
verses.dgt: blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will certainly not count.”

verses.greek: Ὁ μακαρισμὸς οὖν οὗτος ἐπὶ τὴν περιτομὴν ἢ καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν ἀκροβυστίαν; λέγομεν γάρ· Ἐλογίσθη τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἡ πίστις εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
verses.literal: Is the blessing then this on the circumcision or also on the uncircumcision? We are saying for was credited the to Abraham the faith as righteousness.
verses.dgt: Is this blessedness, then, for the circumcised or also for the uncircumcised? For we say, “Faith was counted to Abraham as righteousness.”

verses.greek: πῶς οὖν ἐλογίσθη; ἐν περιτομῇ ὄντι ἢ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ; οὐκ ἐν περιτομῇ ἀλλʼ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ·
verses.literal: How then was it credited? In circumcision being or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision but in uncircumcision
verses.dgt: How then was it counted? While he was circumcised or uncircumcised? Not while circumcised, but while uncircumcised.

verses.greek: καὶ σημεῖον ἔλαβεν περιτομῆς, σφραγῖδα τῆς δικαιοσύνης τῆς πίστεως τῆς ἐν τῇ ἀκροβυστίᾳ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν πατέρα πάντων τῶν πιστευόντων διʼ ἀκροβυστίας, εἰς τὸ λογισθῆναι αὐτοῖς τὴν δικαιοσύνην,
verses.literal: And the sign he received of circumcision a seal of the righteousness of the faith that he had while in the uncircumcision for the to be him father of all those believing in uncircumcision for the to be credited to them the righteousness
verses.dgt: And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had while uncircumcised, so that he might be the father of all who believe while uncircumcised, so that righteousness might also be counted to them,

verses.greek: καὶ πατέρα περιτομῆς τοῖς οὐκ ἐκ περιτομῆς μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς στοιχοῦσιν τοῖς ἴχνεσιν τῆς ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ πίστεως τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀβραάμ.
verses.literal: and father of circumcision to those not of circumcision only but also to those walking in the steps the during uncircumcision faith of the father of us Abraham.
verses.dgt: and the father of the circumcised, to those not only from circumcision but also walking in the footsteps of the faith our father Abraham had while uncircumcised.

verses.greek: Οὐ γὰρ διὰ νόμου ἡ ἐπαγγελία τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἢ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ, τὸ κληρονόμον αὐτὸν εἶναι κόσμου, ἀλλὰ διὰ δικαιοσύνης πίστεως·
verses.literal: Not for through the Law was the promise the to Abraham or to the descendants of him that heir he being world but through the righteousness of faith.
verses.dgt: For the promise to Abraham or to his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not through law, but through the righteousness of faith.

verses.greek: εἰ γὰρ οἱ ἐκ νόμου κληρονόμοι, κεκένωται ἡ πίστις καὶ κατήργηται ἡ ἐπαγγελία·
verses.literal: If for those of the Law are heirs has been made void the faith and has been nullified the promise
verses.dgt: For if those from law are heirs, faith has been emptied and the promise has been nullified.

verses.greek: ὁ γὰρ νόμος ὀργὴν κατεργάζεται, οὗ δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν νόμος, οὐδὲ παράβασις.
verses.literal: the For law wrath brings where now no there is law neither is transgression.
verses.dgt: For the law produces wrath, but where there is no law there is also no transgression.

verses.greek: Διὰ τοῦτο ἐκ πίστεως, ἵνα κατὰ χάριν, εἰς τὸ εἶναι βεβαίαν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν παντὶ τῷ σπέρματι, οὐ τῷ ἐκ τοῦ νόμου μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τῷ ἐκ πίστεως Ἀβραάμ (ὅς ἐστιν πατὴρ πάντων ἡμῶν,
verses.literal: Therefore it is of faith that it may be according to grace for the to be sure the promise to all the seed not to that of the law only but also to that of the faith of Abraham who is the father of all of us —
verses.dgt: For this reason it is from faith, so that it may be according to grace, in order that the promise may be certain to all the offspring—not only to those from the law but also to those from Abraham’s faith, who is father of us all,

verses.greek: καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε), κατέναντι οὗ ἐπίστευσεν θεοῦ τοῦ ζῳοποιοῦντος τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ καλοῦντος τὰ μὴ ὄντα ὡς ὄντα·
verses.literal: even as it has been written that A father of many nations I have made you before whom he believed God who is giving life to the dead and calling the things not into being as existing
verses.dgt: just as it is written, “I have appointed you father of many nations,” before the God whom he believed, the one who gives life to the dead and calls the things not existing as though they exist.

verses.greek: ὃς παρʼ ἐλπίδα ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι ἐπίστευσεν εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτὸν πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον· Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου·
verses.literal: who against hope in hope believed for the to become him the father of many nations according to that spoken So will be the offspring of you
verses.dgt: Against hope, in hope he believed, so that he might become father of many nations according to what had been said, “So shall your offspring be.”

verses.greek: καὶ μὴ ἀσθενήσας τῇ πίστει κατενόησεν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ σῶμα νενεκρωμένον, ἑκατονταετής που ὑπάρχων, καὶ τὴν νέκρωσιν τῆς μήτρας Σάρρας,
verses.literal: And not having become weak in the faith he considered the his own body expired a hundred years old about being and the lifelessness of the womb of Sarah
verses.dgt: And without becoming weak in faith, he considered his own body as good as dead, being about a hundred years old, and the deadness of Sarah’s womb.

verses.greek: εἰς δὲ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ θεοῦ οὐ διεκρίθη τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἀλλὰ ἐνεδυναμώθη τῇ πίστει, δοὺς δόξαν τῷ θεῷ
verses.literal: About however the promise the of God not he did waver the through unbelief but was strengthened the in faith having given glory the to God
verses.dgt: But regarding the promise of God he did not waver in unbelief, but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to God

verses.greek: καὶ πληροφορηθεὶς ὅτι ὃ ἐπήγγελται δυνατός ἐστιν καὶ ποιῆσαι.
verses.literal: and having been fully assured that what He has promised able He is also to do
verses.dgt: and being fully assured that what he had promised he was also able to do.

verses.greek: διὸ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
verses.literal: Therefore it was credited to him unto righteousness.
verses.dgt: Therefore it was also counted to him as righteousness.

verses.greek: Οὐκ ἐγράφη δὲ διʼ αὐτὸν μόνον ὅτι ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ,
verses.literal: Not it was written now on account of him alone that it was credited to him
verses.dgt: Now it was not written for his sake alone that it was counted to him,

verses.greek: ἀλλὰ καὶ διʼ ἡμᾶς οἷς μέλλει λογίζεσθαι, τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν ἐγείραντα Ἰησοῦν τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν ἐκ νεκρῶν,
verses.literal: but also on account of us to whom it is about to be credited to those believing on the One having raised Jesus the Lord of us out from the dead
verses.dgt: but also for our sake, to whom it is about to be counted—to us who believe in the one who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,

verses.greek: ὃς παρεδόθη διὰ τὰ παραπτώματα ἡμῶν καὶ ἠγέρθη διὰ τὴν δικαίωσιν ἡμῶν.
verses.literal: who was delivered over for the trespasses of us and was raised for the justification of us.
verses.dgt: who was handed over because of our trespasses and was raised because of our justification.
